newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm, market seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm, market seen stable.

text.p: Some leading Russian shares and second-tier oil stocks edged up on Friday on demand from Russian banks and some Western investors, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 2.16 percent to 292.67 on $31.89 million in volume.
Traders forecast that widening demand from local banks, stable buying interest from the West and some sales from both sides would provide for a stable market next week.
"The market is quite stable," said Rinaco-Plus head of equity trading Andrei Kukk. "There is enough local money to smooth any sharp fluctuations."
Traders said Western sales were not massive and based on asset reallocation within Russian shares.

They said most Western sales were in oil producers LUKoil and Surgutneftegaz and utility Mosenergo. LUKoil closed at $14.800 after $14.955 at Thursday's close, Mosenergo fell to $1.455 from $1.460 and Surgutneftegaz ticked up to $0.597 after $0.594.
"Buy orders are limited and sales orders are at market prices. That's why no one will sell cheaply, but you can buy dear, especially given that prices may rise further," Kukk said.
"But there is Western money, and it is obvious," he added.
Traders said a new big Western fund on the Russian market was buying UES agressively and ordinary shares of the utility rose to $0.1830 from $0.1700, UES priliveged was $0.1410 after $0.1314.
Rostelekom rose to $3.66 from $3.62, Orenburgneft rose to $4.25 from $4.09 and Purneftegaz firmed to $3.70 after $3.54 at Wednesday's close when it was last traded.
